title: model loading breadcrumbs — weights download / sharding failure
content:
Quick scratchpad / breadcrumbs for the model load failures seen on ded-01 (Nov 3-5) — keeping timelines and exact commands so we can reproduce and write a remediation.

Symptom summary:
- Affected: ded-01 serving pool (p100s), model: open-instruct-v1.2 (sharded checkpoint)
- Failure mode: node fails to instantiate model -> process exits during weights load with corrupted checkpoint/IO errors; intermittent; roughly 30% of cold starts.
- Observed first at 2025-11-03 09:12 PDT after rolling change to S3 bucket migration (s3://redwood-models-v2).

What I tried (commands + outputs):
1) Basic curl download (from ded-01) to validate object integrity:
$ aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models-v2/open-instruct-v1.2/weights-00001.pt ./weights-00001.pt
Completed OK (size 2.0GB).
sha256sum weights-00001.pt -> 7f3b2a... (matches manifest)

2) Full checkpoint download + load (local python quick-check):
$ python -c "import torch; torch.load('weights-00001.pt', map_location='cpu')"
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/serialization.py", line 611, in load
    return _legacy_load(opened_file, map_location)
RuntimeError: unexpected EOF while reading file

Notes: ran twice, first time succeeded on ded-01-3, second time failed with EOF. S3 GETs look fine at OS level. Suspect partial reads when many parallel downloads happening (burst).

3) Using multipart download with aws cli (to avoid transient failures) -> still intermittent EOF during torch.load.
4) Attempted verifying object integrity via aws s3api head-object -> ContentLength matches; ETag matches manifest; still torch complains.

5) Reproduced failure in containerized env (local devbox) by generating artificial race: start 8 parallel torch.load processes while copying file over network -> saw same EOF error in ~40% of runs.
Command used to simulate:
$ for i in {1..8}; do python -c "import torch; torch.load('shared/weights-00001.pt'); print('ok', $i)" & done
-> Multiple EOFs, suggests concurrent file I/O + mmap interacting with incomplete file visibility.

6) Switched runtime to use streaming loader (torch.load with file-like object) -> success stable for repeated runs. But our serving runtime uses an mmap-backed loader for performance; switching to streaming regresses perf.

Error snippets captured from runtime logs (redwood-runtime):
[2025-11-04T14:22:11.324Z] ERROR model_loader: failed to map shard weights-00001.pt: RuntimeError("unexpected EOF while reading file")
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/loader.py", line 210, in load_shard
    state = torch.load(shard_path, map_location=device)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/serialization.py", line 611, in load
    return _legacy_load(opened_file, map_location)
RuntimeError: unexpected EOF while reading file

Hypotheses: (ordered by plausibility)
- Hypothesis A: S3 eventual consistency window after bucket migration creates short-lived partial object visibility for range requests / streaming reads under heavy concurrency. Some processes start reading before object fully persisted on edge cache.
- Hypothesis B: Client-side file writes are racing with reads: our downloader writes file via tempfile -> atomic rename? If not atomic on the remote FS, mmap/readers could hit partial file. We use move-from-temp during download but some code path may call loader before rename completes.
- Hypothesis C: Checkpoint sharding format mismatch: some older checkpoints (legacy format) include a trailing metadata blob that torch expects differently—corruption shows as EOF. Less likely since sha256 matches manifest.
- Hypothesis D: Filesystem (ephemeral overlay on ded-01) mmap semantics broken under high concurrency leading to reads that get truncated.

Evidence supporting A/B:
- Failures correlate with deploy window and S3 bucket migration timing.
- Local repro via concurrent access suggests client-side read/write race or concurrent mmap issues.
- head-object & sha256 checks were OK when downloaded fully; intermittent EOF implies partial read windows not integrity mismatch.

Quick checks to run next (short term):
- Add a post-download checksum verification step (sha256) before exposing file to loader. If checksum missing -> don't load.
- Ensure downloader writes to temp path + atomic rename. Double-check code paths that signal "download complete" to loader. Search for direct write-to-final-path uses.
- Try forcing range/get with s3 cli with --no-verify-ssl? (not relevant) — instead add 1s sleep after rename to test race.
- Reproduce under load with strace to confirm read behavior and whether loader opens file before rename completes.
- Try switch loader to open(file, 'rb') and stream into torch.load(io.BytesIO(data)) as a canary for weeks to estimate perf impact.

Longer-term mitigation ideas:
- Add integrity gating: only move file into /models/ready after checksum verified. Loader only scans ready/ dir. Add lock file semantics.
- Add per-shard exponential backoff + retry on EOF during load (fast fail then retry) — cheap mitigation.
- Use S3 object tagging + post-commit notification (SQS) so edge caches have time to sync after large object writes (maybe heavy).
- Consider switching to signed-manifest approach: downloader writes .inprogress + on success writes manifest and atomically renames. Loader checks manifest.

Notes from Maya (chat): "noticed that the downloader process sometimes returns 0 before rename on k8s mount?" -> ask infra if NFS overlay settings cause rename semantics to be non-atomic across pods.

Immediate plan (next 48h):
- Add checksum gating + quick retry on EOF in loader (PR to runtime). Owner: Ryan (today).
- Run simulated stress harness (8-16 parallel loads) on ded-01 under s3-v2 bucket to repro. Owner: Jordan (tomorrow).
- Infra to validate NFS/mount options on ded pools for rename atomicity. Owner: Infra team (request sent).

Open questions / TODO:
- Is the downloader already doing atomic rename in all code paths? grep for os.replace / rename vs open(final_path) writes.
- Do we have a reproducible pattern to trigger EOF (file size threshold / object >1GB)? I saw more failures on >1GB objects.
- What is the exact interaction with our mmap path vs streaming path (we should add metrics for counts of mmap vs streaming loads and failure rates).

Raw commands / diagnostics that were useful: (copy to ticket)
- aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models-v2/open-instruct-v1.2/weights-00001.pt ./ && sha256sum weights-00001.pt
- python -c "import torch; torch.load('weights-00001.pt', map_location='cpu')"  # shows EOF
- strace -f -e trace=open,read,rename -p <pid>  # watch for rename ordering
- lsof + grep weights-00001.pt  # who has file open

If anyone hits this in the wild, please paste stderr from loader and the sha256 of the downloaded file + the downloader PID. That helps narrow whether it was a partial download vs format mismatch.

-- ryan
